text:
raj: Seeing flaky eval CI for the quantized-llama nightly job — metrics jump around between runs. Anyone else seeing non-deterministic outputs?
anya: yep, started noticing yesterday. CI pass rates for perplexity/regression tests bounce even with no model or harness change :grimacing:
raj: pasted small excerpt of two runs — same prompt, different sampled tokens. Our harness sets seed but we use sampling tests too, so seed should force determinism.
raj: config snippet:
```
# eval_runner config
runner = EvalRunner(seed=42, deterministic=False)
sampling = {"temperature": 0.0, "top_p": 1.0}  # want greedy but still running sampling path for other tests
```
matt: I can repro locally intermittently when quantized kernels are enabled and batch_size>1. Looks like RNG state isn't consistent across worker threads — sometimes workers get seeded from /dev/urandom when spawned.
anya: digging in the runner: we seed the main process early but worker pool threads call into C++ quantized libs which create their own RNG state on first use. If worker pool is created lazily per test, different runs lead to different per-worker seeds. Proposed: explicitly propagate seed to workers after pool creation.
raj: I'll try a patch that seeds workers immediately and also add a deterministic_ci flag to force eager pool creation in CI.
julie: Could also add a "hermetic" mode for eval harness that forces greedy decoding and single-threaded exec to establish a stable baseline for regression detection, even if it differs from prod perf.
matt: opened PR with tests: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/merge_requests/2123 — adds a small harness that runs identical prompt 5x and asserts outputs equal when deterministic=true, plus seed propagation logic.
ci-bot: Build 1245 started for branch raj/seed-worker-fix.
raj: Ran extended local job with quantized lib + batch_size=4 x 50 trials — stable now. Pushing PR to run in CI.
anya: after merge, can we surface an eval variance metric in the dashboard? e.g., per-model-per-metric stddev over N trials — alert if > threshold. That would catch other nondeterminism like sampling param mismatches or kernel fallbacks.
julie: +1 on dashboarding and link run artifacts to failing alerts. We should also log kernel fallback events (float->quantized) to correlate with output variance.
matt: note for post-merge: add a CI job that runs quantized nightly in hermetic mode to avoid noisy CI blips during normal PRs.
raj: thanks all — will update PR with worker-seed tests and CI job. If anyone wants to help debug kernel-level RNG, ping me.
